recommendations.title: Retain the data-protection compliance anchor for data sharing
recommendations.rationale:
- ED S 1.3 requires sharing in "full compliance with the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 and other relevant data privacy and protection requirements".
- HKMA clause 34.3.2(i) requires parties to "comply with the applicable laws and guidance on the protection of personal data".
- The draft's anchor matches the peer baseline and grounds the third-party obligations in S 11.8.
recommendations.action: Keep S 1.3 as the governing data-protection requirement and retain the S 11.8 obligation that third-party service providers comply with data privacy, confidentiality and security rules.

recommendations.title: Retain the real-time consent dashboard requirement
recommendations.rationale:
- ED S 10.4 requires the consent dashboard to reflect "the real-time status of consent and is updated immediately upon any renewal, revocation or expiration".
- The HKMA framework sets no equivalent dashboard requirement.
- This enhancement exceeds the peer baseline and should be kept.
recommendations.action: Retain S 10.4 as drafted, requiring the consent dashboard to show real-time status updated immediately on renewal, revocation or expiration.

recommendations.title: Add a customer-liability standard for unauthorised transactions
recommendations.rationale:
- HKMA clause 50 provides a customer "should not be responsible for any direct loss" from unauthorised transactions absent fraud or gross negligence.
- ED S 11.12 covers assistance, complaints handling and redress but sets no liability standard.
- Without an explicit standard, customers lack certainty on loss allocation.
recommendations.action: Add a provision fixing customer liability for unauthorised transactions, aligned with the redress mechanisms already in S 11.12.

recommendations.title: Retain the firm mandatory commencement dates for FSP obligations
recommendations.rationale:
- ED S 9.1 ties obligations to "the timeline specified in Appendix 2" and S 9.2 fixes a 1 January 2028 date.
- HKMA clause 19 leaves timing to banks, treating dates as "the latest expected dates".
- The draft's firm dates give clearer, enforceable transition arrangements.
recommendations.action: Keep the concrete commencement dates in S 9.1 and S 9.2 and Appendix 2 rather than adopting the HKMA advisory-timeline approach.

recommendations.title: Add test environments and sample data to support participants
recommendations.rationale:
- HKMA clause 52.4 requires banks to "provide examples and testing environment with data (including artificial customer data if necessary)".
- ED S 12.5 requires FSPs to meet platform technology requirements but sets no test-environment obligation.
- Without test facilities, data consumers face higher integration risk.
recommendations.action: Add a requirement that platform participants provide test environments and sample data, or confirm this sits with the platform operator under S 12.5.

recommendations.title: Retain uniform cyber and API security controls across activities
recommendations.rationale:
- ED S 12.3 requires "robust API security controls" and cyber measures across all open finance activities.
- HKMA clause 12 varies protections progressively by the four API categories.
- Uniform controls avoid gaps that a category-tiered approach can leave.
recommendations.action: Keep S 12.2 and S 12.3 applying cyber and API security controls uniformly rather than tiering protections by data category.

recommendations.title: Retain independent third-party management over shared assessments
recommendations.rationale:
- ED S 12.2 requires "robust third-party service provider management" as part of technology operations.
- HKMA clause 31.3.1 lets a bank rely on a TSP "successfully assessed by another bank".
- The draft's independent standard reduces reliance on assessments the FSP did not perform.
recommendations.action: Keep S 12.2 requiring each FSP to manage third-party risk directly, without a provision permitting reliance on another participant's assessment.

recommendations.rationale:
- ED S 8.1 conditions participation on meeting Policy Document and platform requirements.
- The draft encourages accessible interface design for underserved customers; the HKMA framework does not.
- This customer-protection feature exceeds the peer baseline and should be kept.
recommendations.action: Retain the encouragement for inclusive, accessible interface design serving underserved customers within the participation requirements.
